near_duplicate_resolution.original_overlap: Both original items asked the nurse to classify a fasting plasma glucose result using diabetes/prediabetes thresholds.
near_duplicate_resolution.resolution: Retain V2-Q1038 as the fasting-plasma-glucose diagnosis/confirmation item and rebuild V2-Q0886 into interpretation of a complete diabetic-ketoacidosis laboratory pattern.

semantic_correction.stem: Four adults with no prior diagnosis of diabetes are being evaluated for a possible hyperglycemic crisis. Which laboratory pattern meets all ADA 2026 diagnostic components for diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA)?

options.A: Glucose 240 mg/dL; β-hydroxybutyrate 3.5 mmol/L; pH 7.28; bicarbonate 17 mmol/L
options.B: Glucose 240 mg/dL; β-hydroxybutyrate 2.0 mmol/L; pH 7.28; bicarbonate 17 mmol/L
options.C: Glucose 240 mg/dL; β-hydroxybutyrate 3.5 mmol/L; pH 7.34; bicarbonate 20 mmol/L
options.D: Glucose 180 mg/dL; β-hydroxybutyrate 3.5 mmol/L; pH 7.28; bicarbonate 17 mmol/L

semantic_correction.rationale: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026 Table 16.1 requires all DKA diagnostic components: diabetes/hyperglycemia defined as glucose at least 200 mg/dL or a prior history of diabetes; ketosis defined as β-hydroxybutyrate at least 3.0 mmol/L or urine ketones at least 2+; and metabolic acidosis defined as pH below 7.3 and/or bicarbonate below 18 mmol/L. Option A satisfies all three components. Option B does not meet the β-hydroxybutyrate ketosis criterion. Option C does not meet the metabolic-acidosis criterion because both pH and bicarbonate are above the DKA cut points. In the stem all clients have no prior diabetes diagnosis, so option D does not satisfy the diabetes/hyperglycemia component because glucose is below 200 mg/dL. Therefore A is the uniquely correct pattern.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Identify diabetic ketoacidosis by integrating the ADA 2026 diabetes/hyperglycemia, ketosis, and metabolic-acidosis diagnostic components rather than relying on a single abnormal laboratory value.
semantic_correction.source_organization: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes
semantic_correction.source_document_title: 16. Diabetes Care in the Hospital: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
semantic_correction.source_locator: Hyperglycemic Crises — Table 16.1 Diagnostic criteria for DKA and HHS

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: resolved semantic near-duplication with V2-Q1038 by replacing a second fasting-glucose classification item with DKA laboratory-pattern recognition; every numeric threshold and option was checked directly against ADA 2026 Table 16.1, and the item was remapped to Reduction of Risk Potential laboratory/diagnostic monitoring.

audit_findings_append.finding: The original item duplicated V2-Q1038's fasting-plasma-glucose threshold interpretation. It was rebuilt into a distinct DKA laboratory-integration item using only directly sourced ADA 2026 cut points.
audit_findings_append.source_authority: ADA Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
audit_findings_append.source_locator: Diabetes Care in the Hospital — Table 16.1
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p. 13 / PDF p. 17

option_audit.A: Correct. Glucose is at least 200 mg/dL, β-hydroxybutyrate is at least 3.0 mmol/L, and both pH and bicarbonate satisfy the metabolic-acidosis component.
option_audit.B: Plausible because hyperglycemia and acidosis are present, but β-hydroxybutyrate 2.0 mmol/L is below the ADA DKA ketosis criterion of 3.0 mmol/L.
option_audit.C: Plausible because hyperglycemia and ketosis are present, but pH 7.34 and bicarbonate 20 mmol/L do not meet the ADA metabolic-acidosis component.
option_audit.D: Plausible because ketosis and acidosis are present, but with no prior diabetes diagnosis the glucose of 180 mg/dL does not meet the ADA diabetes/hyperglycemia component.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. The stem explicitly states no prior diabetes diagnosis, so D cannot use the alternative prior-diabetes route to satisfy the first component; A alone meets all three ADA components.

cueing_check.note: All choices use the same four laboratory fields and identical structure. Equality results from the clinically parallel data format, not added explanatory padding.

blueprint_audit.entry_level_relevance: The item requires an RN to integrate abnormal diagnostic laboratory findings and recognize an acute complication, directly aligned with Reduction of Risk Potential.
